extracted.intended_audience: authors, reviewers, editors, publishers, and other stakeholders in scholarly publishing
extracted.subtask_description: Describes the development and purpose of a standardized terminology (ANSI/NISO Z39.106-2023) for peer review, aimed at harmonizing definitions and increasing transparency across peer review models so stakeholders can understand and participate productively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review is the process of evaluating academic, scientific, or professional work. It is ubiquitously used by academic journals to support research integrity by filtering out invalid or poor-quality articles, as well as to ensure that research outcomes are exposed to relevant audiences through their publication in relevant journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framed as a crucial process in scholarly communication and a pillar of the scientific method; emphasizes both quality control (filtering invalid/poor work) and dissemination (exposing outcomes to relevant audiences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for harmonized nomenclature
rubrics_metrics.description: Over recent decades, a significant number of new peer review models have been introduced (most notably for open review), but they have not been accompanied by the development of a clear and consistent nomenclature, leading to confusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: STM formed a Working Group to harmonize and create improved definitions of discrete elements of peer review processes so community members can quickly and easily recognize how to participate productively; this motivated formal standardization efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and openness as evaluative desiderata
rubrics_metrics.description: There is increased support for more openness and transparency in science and research, including peer review, in order to maintain trust in the scholarly ecosystem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency and openness are presented as essential elements of open research and as objectives that standardized terminology should support to maintain community trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardization via ANSI/NISO Z39.106-2023
rubrics_metrics.description: The formal ANSI/NISO standard, Z39.106-2023, Standard Terminology for Peer Review, resulted from STM and NISO efforts including a pilot program and a NISO public comment period, which led to various adjustments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates that community feedback (pilot programs and public comments) informed the final standard; implies that adoption of this standard is the recommended approach to reduce confusion and enable consistent communication about peer review practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ongoing community support and adoption guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The NISO Peer Review Terminology Standing Committee is supporting this work, providing publicity and further information, answering any questions, and serving as a general community resource for adoption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical support is available (contact nisohq@niso.org) for organizations seeking guidance on how to get started with adopting the terminology; frames the committee as a resource to facilitate uptake and consistent use of the standard.
